fullPassage:
Eiffel Tower Effect

Have you ever heard of the "Eiffel Tower Effect?" When the Eiffel Tower was first built, the iron tower was very different from all the other architecture in Paris, which was mainly made of stone. Many local people disliked the tower and complained that it would ruin the beauty of Paris. Nevertheless, as the locals became familiar with the tower due to exposure, they became more and more fond of it, referring to it as the Tower of Love. This effect, also called the "Mere Exposure Effect," is found with people, too. Psychologist Robert Zajonc and his colleagues showed university students pictures of several faces. Some pictures were shown 25 times while others were shown only once or twice. Then, the students were shown a picture and asked to express how much they liked that person. The students liked the people they had seen more often better than those they had seen less frequently. This shows that the more we are exposed to something, the more favorably we view it.

Nevertheless, as the locals became (C)[familiar / unfamiliar] with the tower due to exposure, they became more and more fond of it. This effect, also called the "Mere Exposure Effect," is found with people, too. Psychologist Robert Zajonc and his colleagues showed university students pictures of several faces. Some pictures were shown 25 times while others were shown only once or twice.

다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오.

Her __________ (familiar) with the neighborhood grew over time. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 그녀의 동네에 대한 친숙함은 시간이 지나면서 커졌다.
det.analysis: ✅ familiarity: 소유격 Her + __________ + with → 명사 필요. familiar(형용사) → familiarity(명사).
det.tip: familiar(형용사: 친숙한) → familiarity(명사: 친숙함).

questions.passage: This shows that the more we are exposed to something, the more (____) we view it. Psychologist Robert Zajonc and his colleagues showed university students pictures of several faces.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오.

The audience reacted __________ (favor) to the new performance. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 관객들은 새 공연에 호의적으로 반응했다.
det.analysis: ✅ favorably: 동사 reacted를 수식 → 부사 필요. favor(명사) → favorable(형용사) → favorably(부사).
det.tip: favor(명사: 호의) → favorable(형용사: 호의적인) → favorably(부사: 호의적으로).

questions.passage:
Eiffel Tower Effect

Have you ever heard of the "Eiffel Tower Effect?" When the Eiffel Tower was first built, the iron tower was very different from all the other architecture in Paris, which was mainly made of stone. Many local people disliked the tower and complained that it would ruin the beauty of Paris. Nevertheless, as the locals became familiar with the tower due to exposure, they became more and more fond of it, ____. This effect, also called the "Mere Exposure Effect," is found with people, too. Psychologist Robert Zajonc and his colleagues showed university students pictures of several faces. Some pictures were shown 25 times while others were shown only once or twice. Then, the students were shown a picture and asked to express how much they liked that person. The students liked the people they had seen more often better than those they had seen less frequently. This shows that the more we are exposed to something, the more favorably we view it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: referring to it as the Tower of Love
refusing to visit it ever again
comparing it to other European towers

det.korean: 탑을 좋아하게 되면서 사랑의 탑이라고 부르게 되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①referring to it as the Tower of Love: 원문 그대로. 호감 증가의 결과. ❌ ②tear it down(철거): 반대. ❌ ③refusing to visit(방문 거부): 반대. ❌ ④comparing(비교): 무관.
det.tip: refer to A as B = A를 B라고 부르다. Tower of Love = 사랑의 탑.

questions.passage:
Eiffel Tower Effect

Have you ever heard of the "Eiffel Tower Effect?" When the Eiffel Tower was first built, the iron tower was very different from all the other architecture in Paris, which was mainly made of stone. Many local people disliked the tower and complained that it would ruin the beauty of Paris. Nevertheless, as the locals became familiar with the tower due to exposure, they became more and more fond of it, referring to it as the Tower of Love. This effect, also called the "Mere Exposure Effect," is found with people, too. Psychologist Robert Zajonc and his colleagues showed university students pictures of several faces. Some pictures were shown 25 times while others were shown only once or twice. Then, the students were shown a picture and asked to express how much they liked that person. The students liked the people they had seen more often better than those they had seen less frequently. This shows that ____.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: first impressions are always the most accurate
people tend to dislike unfamiliar things permanently
the more we are exposed to something, the more favorably we view it

det.korean: 더 많이 노출될수록 더 호의적으로 바라본다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 첫인상: 반대 (반복 노출이 핵심).
❌ ② 영구적 비호감: 반대 (노출로 호감 변화).
❌ ③ 외모: 언급 없음.
✅ ④ 원문 결론 그대로: 노출 빈도와 호감도의 비례 관계. ← 정답
det.tip: the more ~ the more ~: ~하면 할수록 더 ~하다. 비교급 강조 구문. 단순 노출 효과의 핵심 결론.
